asks for each enabled plugin. installed_for already works for any name@marketplace key, so the filter is the only

nothing about superpowers@claude-plugins-official. Expected (brief: "reports FIX naming each plugin the project's

pass_cases: 1. enabledPlugins {"sdd@relay": true, "superpowers@claude-plugins-official": true}, empty registry -> doctor has

details: PLAUSIBLE for the order (whether `claude plugin install` resolves the marketplace from the project's
extraKnownMarketplaces is not shown); CONFIRMED by reading that the detail is discarded (`runner(root, key)[0]`).
Correct today in the common case (relay installed first by `relay install`). Size: 5 minutes.
evidence: lib/relay_setup.py:371 `elif runner(root, key)[0]:` ; :374 todo text without detail; :382 marketplace todo appended last.
failing_case: Fresh machine, relay marketplace not yet added: `relay setup ~/new --flow openspec`. run_plugin_install returns
(False, "<claude's error, e.g. marketplace relay not found>"); setup keeps only [0], so todo item 1 says
"sdd@relay is enabled but not installed ... run `claude plugin install sdd@relay --scope project`" with no reason,
and the `/plugin marketplace add` step is the last item. Run in order, item 1 fails again.
Expected: the todo carries the reason, and the install line follows the marketplace step (or says to do it first).
fix_hint: Keep `ok, why = runner(root, key)` and append `(claude said: {why})` when why is not empty; run the install loop after
merge_user_settings, or word the todo "after step <marketplace add>".
pass_cases: 1. runner returns (False, "marketplace relay not found") -> the sdd todo line contains "marketplace relay not found"
2. runner returns (False, "") -> the todo line still names the exact command (today's test).
3. runner returns (True, "") -> no sdd todo line; done has "installed sdd@relay at project scope" (today's test).
findings.summary: a failed install drops the runner's reason and its todo comes before the marketplace step it may depend on
